posts.note: ProLiv Rx approval announcement plus a neuromodulation glossary. Three items are third-party announcements relayed from RAMHT-AI 2026 (Beckley Clinical, NRx); two are regulatory pipeline items with no asserted outcome.

Cost-effectiveness argument for Medicaid TMS coverage. Almost all past analysis and quoted studies; only the closing presumption of coverage policy changes logged. Title is normative (should be covered).
Satirical eulogy; the underlying thesis (private practice psychiatry is finished, centers are the future) reads as sincere.
Career advice. Imminent ProLiv Rx launch (Neurolief, CONTROL) and one generic go-to-market claim logged. Generic startup truisms not logged.
Review of a pilot dTMS trial in TRS; only a hedged follow-up-worthiness claim logged.
69-word share of a colleague's TMS explainer; no forward-looking claims.
Domain rating post; no forward-looking claims beyond a sign-off.
Press roundup for ProLiv Rx; present-tense results and a quoted mechanism guess by Chris Aiken, no forecasts.
Press roundup; parenting tips and a quoted selection-effect comment, no forecasts.
PTSD explainer with a treatment pipeline section. One Acacia Clinics item (CONTROL candidate).
Reaction to the PBM transparency title of CA 2026. Dense with calls about the end of the PBM business model, with hedged self-doubt near the end.
Evernorth/Cigna dropping TMS prior authorization from March 6, 2026. One Radial item (CONTROL candidate).

statements.quote: CEO of Beckley Clinical previewed 4 payors enganged and interested in covering their deployment of Ketamine-Assisted Therapy
statements.context: Recap of RAMHT-AI 2026 announcements. Josh Stevens (CEO, Beckley Clinical) said four payors are engaged and interested in covering Beckley's ketamine-assisted therapy deployment; the author relays it and calls Stevens a personal friend.
statements.note: Third-party announcement relayed, not adopted; implies future payer coverage of KAT. Author discloses personal friendship.

statements.quote: not only is KetaFree submitted to the FDA to be approved as an on-label ketamine treatment
statements.context: RAMHT-AI 2026 recap. Jonathan Javitt (CEO, NRx) announced that KetaFree has been submitted to the FDA for approval as an on-label ketamine treatment. Regulatory pipeline item; no outcome asserted by the author.
statements.note: Pipeline status relayed from NRx CEO; implies a pending FDA decision. No approval call made.

statements.quote: have partnered with with Neurocare to bring neuroplastic therapies for bipolar and unipolar depression to scale
statements.context: Same NRx announcement: NRx has other neuroplastogens in development and has partnered with Neurocare to scale neuroplastic therapies for bipolar and unipolar depression.
statements.note: Third-party partnership intent relayed by the author. Compound sentence with the KetaFree submission.

statements.quote: and maybe necessary for OCD, essential tremor, and dystonia, as well as other conditions in the future, like depression
statements.context: Glossary entry for DBS (deep brain stimulation). The author says DBS is necessary for Parkinson's and may be necessary for OCD, essential tremor, dystonia, and, in the future, other conditions such as depression.
statements.note: Hedged expectation that DBS use extends to depression.

statements.quote: is going through an FDA breakthrough process for PTSD
statements.context: Glossary entry for nVNS. The GammaCore device is FDA-labeled for migraine, hemicrania continua and cluster headache and, per the author, is going through an FDA breakthrough process for PTSD.
statements.note: Regulatory pipeline status; no outcome asserted. Logged for the coder's judgment.

statements.quote: I’m looking forward to new data on large scale replication trials that should be published soon.
statements.context: Glossary entry for eTNS (Monarch eTNS device, FDA-cleared breakthrough device for refractory seizures and ADHD in youth). The author expects large-scale replication trial data to be published soon.
statements.note: Publication timing call for eTNS replication trials.

statements.quote: Thanks for reading, and if you run a Medicaid Plan, I thank you for your coverage policy changes in advance!
statements.context: Closing line of an argument that TMS is cost-effective and should be covered by state Medicaid plans. The author presumes, half-jokingly, that Medicaid plan administrators will change coverage policy for TMS.
statements.note: Rhetorical presumption of future Medicaid TMS coverage changes; borderline wish. The post title is normative (should be covered).

statements.quote: The talkiatrists would prescribe the pills just fine—maybe some of us would sell to out to deathstance health, and get out while we could. Maybe we’d built a center too?
statements.context: Satirical eulogy for psychiatric private practice. The author expects some psychopharmacology private practitioners to sell to LifeStance ('deathstance health') or build treatment centers.
statements.note: Satirical framing; underlying consolidation claim reads sincere. 'deathstance health' is a jab at LifeStance.

statements.quote: The Center was the future, not the Private Practice.
statements.context: Satirical eulogy. After noting that about 600 Spravato Centers generated $2 billion last year, the author states that treatment centers, not private practices, are the future of outpatient psychiatry.
statements.note: Past-tense eulogy voice; sincere claim about the direction of the outpatient psychiatry business model.

statements.quote: And some did, and some will, but the privacy of our practices make them unappealing, unnoticed, unplatformed, and patients wanted us to take insurance, too. It, quite simply, won’t do.
statements.context: Satirical eulogy conclusion. The author says some psychiatrists will build centers or sell out, but the private practice model will not survive because it is unplatformed and out-of-network.
statements.note: Core thesis of the eulogy: psychiatric private practice is finished. Satirical framing, sincere claim.

statements.quote: Join the waitlist for the ( imminent) device launch here.
statements.context: Section on the author's current roles. As CMO of Neurolief, he links a waitlist and calls the ProLiv Rx device launch imminent (device FDA-approved at the end of 2025).
statements.note: Own-organization claim (Neurolief); coder likely marks CONTROL.

statements.quote: Some of this experience should be outpatient, because that is more likely to be where innovative companies will bring their products to market.
statements.context: Career advice section. The author expects innovative brain-medicine companies to bring products to market in outpatient settings, so recommends outpatient experience.
statements.note: Generic, hedged claim about where new products launch; the 'should' is advice, the predictive clause is the logged part.

statements.quote: if you accept that a treatment that could be the opposite of antidepressant might make some people feel worse, and still be potentially biologically active? Well, then this pilot might be worth following up on.
statements.context: Review of a pilot RCT of 1 Hz deep TMS (BrainsWay H7 coil) over the anterior cingulate in treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Despite dropouts for symptom aggravation, the author suggests the inhibitory dTMS approach may be biologically active and merits follow-up trials.
statements.note: Borderline: hedged judgment that further trials are warranted; no outcome predicted.

statements.quote: There is hope for PTSD, available both now and more coming soon.
statements.context: Transition into the treatment section of a PTSD explainer. The author says more PTSD treatments are coming soon, then lists pipeline items (ibogaine, COMP360, fMRI-guided TMS).
statements.note: General pipeline call for PTSD treatments.

statements.quote: Compass has submitted to the FDA for a COMP360 indication in PTSD as well.
statements.context: PTSD treatment section. The author states that Compass Pathways has submitted COMP360 (psilocybin) to the FDA for a PTSD indication. Regulatory pipeline item; no outcome asserted.
statements.note: Pipeline status claim implying a pending FDA decision; the author makes no approval call.

statements.quote: did breathaking work on Ibogaine and it’s potential (combined with magnesium for safety) for PTSD in co-occuring TBI
statements.context: PTSD treatment section. The author endorses the late Nolan Williams's work on ibogaine (with magnesium) as having potential for PTSD with co-occurring TBI.
statements.note: Borderline: soft endorsement of therapeutic potential, not a dated call.

statements.quote: Shan Siddiqi, M.D., is studying PTSD specific fMRI-guided accelerated TMS as we speak, to make this available at scale, along with colleagues from Acacia Clinics.
statements.context: PTSD treatment section. Shan Siddiqi and colleagues at Acacia Clinics are studying PTSD-specific fMRI-guided accelerated TMS with the aim of making it available at scale.
statements.note: Acacia is one of the author's organizations; coder likely marks CONTROL. Stated aim, not an outcome call.

statements.quote: And, as soon as this law kicks into force in 2028, it will no longer be the status quo.
statements.context: Reaction to the PBM provisions (Title VII) of the 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act signed the night before. The author says the PBM rebate and formulary tiering status quo ends when the law takes effect in 2028.
statements.note: Dated call tied to the law's effective date.

statements.quote: in my opinion, completely destroyed the financial rationale for PBMs as a profit center for giant healthcare conglomerates
statements.context: Assessment of CA 2026's full rebate pass-through and fiduciary provisions. The author says the law destroys the financial rationale for PBMs as profit centers of large insurers (Cigna/Express Scripts, UnitedHealth/OptumRx, CVS/Caremark).
statements.note: Implies PBMs stop being the most profitable part of the conglomerates (post title).

statements.quote: I'm a little surprised the share price of major insurance companies like UnitedHealth Group did not drop a stone today
statements.context: After reading the PBM transparency provisions, the author expresses surprise that UnitedHealth Group and similar insurer shares did not fall, implying he expects the law to hurt their valuations once understood.
statements.note: Implicit market call; the author hedges ('Either I'm missing something, or everybody else is').

statements.quote: The PBM game is up.
statements.context: Flat call after describing the 30-month contract renewal ban and disclosure rules in CA 2026: the PBM business model is finished.
statements.note: Unhedged; contrast with the hedged 'I don't know if this is gonna actually change things' later in the same post.

statements.quote: CA2026 provide provides the kind of transparency that no racket can withstand.
statements.context: Analogy: CA 2026 is to PBM business models what RICO was to the Mafia. The author says the law's transparency will end the PBM 'racket'.
statements.note: Restates 'The PBM game is up' via the RICO analogy.

statements.quote: But is catastrophic is the requirement for 100% of rebates to be passed on to the health plan.
statements.context: Penalties section. The author says the fines ($10,000/day, $100,000 per false item) are not catastrophic, but the 100 percent rebate pass-through requirement is catastrophic for PBM economics.
statements.note: Impact assessment of a provision that takes effect later; typo in source preserved.

statements.quote: And that's…all over with.
statements.context: After describing how PBM reports bundled drugs into opaque categories (e.g. 'antipsychotics' mixing $2 and $2000 drugs), the author says that practice is over under CA 2026.
statements.note: Call that opaque category-level PBM reporting ends.

statements.quote: I don't know if this is gonna actually change things, I've lived in this country and dealt with American healthcare long enough to know that the status quote is gonna fight to preserve itself. I just don't know if they have the juice anymore.
statements.context: Hedge near the end of the PBM post. The author expects incumbents to fight the law and is uncertain whether CA 2026 will change PBM practice.
statements.note: Compound: (a) the status quo will fight back, (b) uncertain whether the law changes things. Softens the earlier 'The PBM game is up'.

statements.quote: PBMs have become radioactive politically, and have become extremely popular for politicians to hate. The worm has turned…maybe.
statements.context: Closing assessment: the political tide has turned against PBMs, hedged with 'maybe'.
statements.note: Hedged turning-point call.

statements.quote: Just last week, another wall came tumbling down: Evernorth, part of Cigna, announced ending prior authorization for TMS (appropriately prescribed) starting in March!
statements.context: The author restates Evernorth Behavioral Health's announcement that prior authorization for TMS ends for in-network providers under Evernorth and Cigna plans effective March 6, 2026.
statements.note: Author's restatement of a company announcement, adopted as fact. The quoted announcement is logged separately.

statements.quote: effective March 6, 2026, prior authorization will no longer be required for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) for Evernorth contracted providers
statements.context: Block quote of the Evernorth Behavioral Health announcement reproduced in the post; it also notes that TMS with dates of service before March 6, 2026 may still need prior authorization.
statements.note: Quoted third-party (Evernorth) text endorsed by the author; duplicates the restatement above with the exact date.

statements.quote: So I think CIGNA is gonna be a more popular plan with physicians, and maybe that means it's gonna be a more popular plan with employers and patients.
statements.context: The author's read on Evernorth/Cigna dropping TMS prior authorization: it is a savvy network strategy that will make Cigna more popular with physicians and perhaps with employers and patients.
statements.note: Compound: physician popularity (firmer) and employer/patient popularity (hedged with 'maybe').

statements.quote: If you have CIGNA as your plan, we can get started on treatment that same day in the very near future.
statements.context: Closing plug for Radial, where the author works: once the Evernorth policy takes effect, Radial expects to start TMS for Cigna members on the same day.
statements.note: Own-organization claim (Radial); coder likely marks CONTROL.
